attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man — the woman — is the folder's own: «καταγόταν από την Τύρο της Συρίας και ήταν κόρη του στρατηγού Ουρβανού (περί το 200 μ.Χ.)», Christina of Tyre, great martyr, as the Romanian «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Hristina» has her. The Greek page adds the year the Romanian source did not give, «περί το 200 μ.Χ.», which is why this upgrade proposes a `dates` object where the folder had none; and it adds the history of her incorrupt relics, from Syria to Constantinople, then to Venice under the Frankish rule, to Torcello in 1252, to Murano in 1340, back to Torcello in 1435 by order of Pope Eugene IV, to the monastery of Saint Justina of Venice in 1793 and in 1810 to the church of San Francesco della Vigna, where the page says they lie now in a crystal reliquary. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints three hymns and all three are taken: a proper apolytikion that names her, a second apolytikion which is the common of a woman martyr, «Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ», printed under her name as «Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον» and therefore her service, and a kontakion that names her.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 06.08.2026 (24. јул ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Христина.“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4). **THE HEADING’S RANK IS LESSER THAN THE ONE THE FOLDER HOLDS, AND THAT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS WAVE HAS MET THAT SHAPE.** «Света» is “saint” and no rank; «мученица» is `martyr` by §5. **The folder holds `great-martyr`**, off saint.gr’s «Η μεγαλομάρτυς» and doxologia’s «Mare Muceniță», and `virgin` beside it. **`martyr` IS NOT ADDED**: it is the same rank at a lower grade, two calendars give the higher one, and a folder reading `great-martyr, martyr` would tell the reader the Church ranks her twice. **Nor is `great-martyr` disturbed**, because this book’s silence on the grade is not a denial of it. `virgin` is untouched and the body corroborates it — the angel «called her a bride of Christ». Recorded, not resolved. **THE DATE IS REFUSED, AND IT IS THE SECOND DATE REFUSAL IN TWO DAYS.** The folder holds `floruit` earliest 190, latest 210, display «c. 200», basis traditional, off saint.gr. This entry ends „Чесно пострада света Христина у III столећу.“ — the holy Christina suffered honourably **in the III century**, which is 201 to 300. **That is neither a point inside the recorded interval nor a statement the interval contains**: 190 to 210 and 201 to 300 overlap only in the ten years 201 to 210, and the book’s claim runs ninety years past the end of the corpus’s. Writing it would be either a widening of a recorded interval or the addition of a `death` field beside a `floruit` that begins before it — and **the narrowing rule of this range licenses neither**: a stated year fills an EMPTY `dates` field, and this field is not empty. A widening is the author’s. Nothing is written and the exact alternative block is named in this batch’s commit message. **THE FOLD THIS FORM MAKES, AND BOTH MEMBERS ARE THIRD-CENTURY MARTYRS NAMED CHRISTINA.** `foldchk.py` measured «Христина» as already held in sr by `christina-martyr-18-may` and `sr-foldpred.mjs` answered `new key, other holders: 1`. **The hazard is real and is not a coincidence of forenames only**: that folder is a `martyr` and `virgin` too, and its `death` is **earliest 201, latest 300, display «3rd century»** — the very century this entry gives for this woman. Two Christinas, both virgin martyrs, both of the third century, two days apart in the calendar. **They are two women, and the dossiers part on everything else**: `christina-martyr-18-may` is named by doxologia with seven holy virgins and by saint.gr in a company with Peter and Dionysius, and is kept on 18 May by three calendars; this woman is the daughter of a governor of Tyre, shut in a tower, whose own father tried her. Read in this batch’s commit message. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS, AND IT IS THE FULLEST ACCOUNT OF HER IN THIS FOLDER. „Родом из града Тира, ћерка намесника царског Урбана, идолопоклоника.“ — **of Tyre, the daughter of the emperor’s governor Урбан, an idolater**. „Не зна се из каквих разлога родитељи њени дадоше јој то име, Христина, но оно скриваше у себи тајну њеног будућег следовања Христу.“ — it is not known why her parents gave her that name, **but it hid in itself the secret of her following Christ to come**, which is the entry’s own frame for the whole story. „До своје једанаесте године она не знаде ништа о Христу. А када јој би 11 година, отац њен, да би је скрио од света због њене изванредне лепоте до потпуног узраста, одреди јој највиши спрат једне високе куле, да ту живи.“ — she knew nothing of Christ until her eleventh year, and then her father, to hide her from the world **on account of her extraordinary beauty until she was fully grown**, set apart for her the highest floor of a tall tower. „Устроји јој све удобности за живот, даде јој робиње на службу, и постави у њене одаје идоле сребрне и златне, да им свакодневно приноси жртве.“, with every comfort, slave-women, and **idols of silver and gold in her rooms to sacrifice to daily**. „Но души младе Христине беше тескобно у тој идолопоклоничкој средини. Гледајући кроз прозор дању у сунце и све красоте света а ноћу у чудесно јато сјајних звезда, она по своме природном разуму дође до чврсте вере у једнога живога Бога.“ — and **looking out of the window by day at the sun and by night at the wonderful flock of shining stars, she came BY HER OWN NATURAL REASON to a firm faith in one living God**, which is the best sentence on the page. „Милостиви Бог, видећи њену чежњу за истином, посла јој ангела свога који је прекрсти крсним знамењем, назва је невестом Христовом и поучи је потпуно у богопознању.“, God sent his angel, who signed her with the cross, called her a bride of Christ and taught her fully. „Тада Христина полупа све идоле у својим одајама, и тиме изазва дивљу јарост код свога оца.“, she broke all the idols to pieces; „Отац је изведе на суд и предаде је мукама а потом баци у тамницу намеравајући, да је сутрадан посече мачем.“, her father tried her, tormented her and jailed her meaning to behead her next day; **and „Но те ноћи здрав читав Урбан изврже душу своју и оде у гроб пре кћери своје.“ — that very night Urban, WHOLE AND IN HEALTH, gave up his soul and went to the grave before his daughter**. „За тим два намесника, Дион и Јулијан, продужише истјазавање ове свете девице.“, two governors, Дион and Јулијан, carried on; „Христинина храброст у трпљењу и чудеса, која почини силом Божјом, обратише многе незнабошце тирске у Хришћанство.“, her courage and her wonders turned many of the heathen of Tyre; „За време мучења Христине Дион наједанпут паде мртав усред народа.“, **Dion fell down dead in the middle of the people during her torture**; and „Његов наследник Јулијан одсече Христини груди и језик. Мученица узе свој језик руком и баци га у очи Јулијану. И овај на једном поста слеп.“ — Julian cut off her breasts and her tongue, **and the martyr took her own tongue in her hand and threw it into Julian’s eyes, and he at once went blind**. „Најзад, муке њене за Христа свршише се смрћу под оштрим мачем, а њен живот продужи се у бесмртном царству ангелском.“, and her torments ended under a sharp sword. **NO `related` ROW, AND THE FOLDER HAD NONE AND KEEPS NONE.** `proseprobe.mjs` over the drafted paragraph returned **`0 name(s) the index would link`**. **THE THREE MEN OF THE ENTRY ALL FAIL RULING 3.** Урбан, her father: `ls saints | grep -i urban` returns `urban-child-martyr`, `urban-of-macedonia`, `urban-the-envoy-of-nicomedia`, `urbanus-8-march` and `urbanus-son-of-gaius`, and **not one of them is a persecutor at all, let alone a governor of Tyre who tried his own daughter** — and a persecutor is in any case nobody’s saint. Дион: the corpus holds `dion`, a martyr of the Greek 8 March, and `dion-of-the-twenty-four-martyrs`, and this Dion is the governor who dropped dead torturing her. Јулијан: more than thirty Julian folders and this one is the man blinded by a severed tongue. None is a saint of this entry and no row is made for any. The slave-women and the converted heathen of Tyre are a household and a crowd. No `office`. No `locations`: Tyre is named and is not written as a coordinate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Hristina, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Mari Mucenițe Hristina», Glasul 4

english.text: Your lamb, Jesus, Christina, cries out with a great voice: You, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking You I am tormented, and I am crucified with You and buried with You in Your baptism; and I suffer for You, that I may reign in You; and I die for You, that I may live for You. But receive me, as a spotless sacrifice, offering myself to You in love. By her prayers, as You are merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Τοῦ πατρός σου τὴν πλάνην λιποῦσα πάνσεμνε, τῆς εὐσεβείας ἐδέξω τὴν θείαν ἔλλαμψιν, καὶ νενύμφευσαι Χριστῷ ὡς καλλιπάρθενος- ὅθεν ἠγώνισαι στερρῶς, καὶ καθεῖλες τὸν ἐχθρόν, Χριστίνα Μεγαλομάρτυς. Καὶ νῦν ἀπαύστως δυσώπει, ἐλεηθήναι τᾶς ψυχᾶς ἠμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the first of three hymns on the page of «Αγία Χριστίνα η μεγαλομάρτυς». It names her and names her father's error, so it is her own proper. Its «ἐλεηθήναι τᾶς ψυχᾶς ἠμῶν» is the page's reading and is copied as it stands

english.text: Leaving behind your father's error, all-revered one, you received the divine radiance of true religion and were betrothed to Christ as a fair virgin; whence you contended steadfastly and cast down the enemy, Christina, great martyr. And now entreat him unceasingly, that our souls may find mercy.

hymns.text: Ἡ ἀμνάς σου Ἰησοῦ, κράζει μεγάλη τῇ φωνῇ. Σὲ Νυμφίε μου ποθῶ, καὶ σὲ ζητοῦσα ἀθλῶ, καὶ συσταυροῦμαι καὶ συνθάπτομαι τῷ βαπτισμῷ σου· καὶ πάσχω διὰ σέ, ὡς βασιλεύσω σὺν σοί, καὶ θνήσκω ὑπὲρ σοῦ, ἵνα καὶ ζήσω ἐν σοί· ἀλλ᾽ ὡς θυσίαν ἄμωμον προσδέχου τὴν μετὰ πόθου τυθεῖσάν σοι. Αὐτῆς πρεσβείαις, ὡς ἐλεήμων, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’ — the second hymn on the page of «Αγία Χριστίνα η μεγαλομάρτυς». It is the common of a woman martyr and names nobody, but the page prints it under her name, so by the corpus's rule it is her service and is copied whole

english.text: Your lamb, O Jesus, cries out with a loud voice: you, my Bridegroom, I long for, and seeking you I contend, and I am crucified and buried with you in your baptism; I suffer for your sake that I may reign with you, and I die for you that I may also live in you. But receive me as a spotless sacrifice, slain for you out of longing. By her intercessions, as you are merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Φωτοειδὴς περιστερὰ ἐγνωρίσθης, ἔχουσα πτέρυγας χρυσᾶς, καὶ πρὸς ὕψος, τῶν οὐρανῶν κατέπαυσας Χριστίνα σεμνή· ὅθεν σου τὴν ἔνδοξον, ἑορτὴν ἐκτελοῦμεν, πίστει προσκυνοῦντές σου, τῶν λειψάνων τὴν θήκην, ἐξ ἧς πηγάζει πᾶσιν ἀληθῶς, ἴαμα θεῖον, ψυχῆς τε καὶ σώματος.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ὁ ὑψωθεῖς — the third hymn on the page of «Αγία Χριστίνα η μεγαλομάρτυς», and it names her and her reliquary

english.text: You were made known as a dove shining with light, having wings of gold, and you came to rest in the height of the heavens, revered Christina; and so we keep your glorious feast, venerating in faith the casket of your relics, out of which there truly springs for all a divine healing of soul and body.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «καταγόταν από την Τύρο της Συρίας και ήταν κόρη του στρατηγού Ουρβανού (περί το 200 μ.Χ.)» — the page's own «about 200», set against her father's generalship; it gives no year of her martyrdom. The folder's Romanian source gave no year at all.
